newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium's Verplaetse sees modest budget reviews.
newsitem.headline: Belgium's Verplaetse sees modest budget reviews.

text.p: Belgian central bank governor Alfons Verplaetse was quoted on Tuesday as saying he expected upcoming budget reviews aimed at keeping Belgium on track for economic and monetary union (EMU), to be modest.

"Today in Belgium the bulk of the budgetary effort has been carried out. To prove it, with a correction of 10 billion francs, the government can comfortably reach the three percent (deficit goal) this year," Verplaetse told Le Soir newspaper.
"And for the next (budget) rounds, I'm expecting adjustments of between five and 10 billion francs. Not more," he said.
The Belgian government approved a 10 billion franc austerity package, aimed at keeping the 1997 deficit on target to hit 2.9 percent of gross domestic product (GDP), in March.
Every spring the Belgian government reviews the budget drafted the previous autumn to make sure it stays on track to meet its targets.
